digo: Chibalazi chanze (also Chibalazi cha nze); Chibalazi mlungu
digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III, App. VI; Mgombato
other_mijikenda: Duruma: Chibalazi mlungu, same name (Pakia App. VI)

teaser.en: A wild pigeon pea that nobody planted: Digo call it God's pigeon pea, or the pigeon pea from outside.
teaser.sw: Mbaazi pori ambayo hakuna aliyeipanda: Wadigo huiita mbaazi ya Mungu, au mbaazi ya nje.

summary.en: *Chibalazi chanze* is a hairy wild legume whose leaves look like those of the cultivated pigeon pea. Both its Digo names say that it grows wild, without anyone planting it.
summary.sw: *Chibalazi chanze* ni mmea wa porini wa jamii ya kunde wenye vinyweleo, ambao majani yake yanafanana na ya mbaazi inayolimwa. Majina yake yote mawili ya Kidigo yanasema kuwa huota porini, bila mtu yeyote kuupanda.

about.en: *Tephrosia villosa* is a low, bushy herb or small shrub of the pea family, covered in soft grey hairs. Its leaves are divided into several pairs of narrow leaflets, rather like a pigeon pea's. It has small pink to purple pea flowers and narrow, hairy pods. Digo pick it out by its leaves.
about.sw: *Tephrosia villosa* ni mmea mfupi wenye matawi mengi au kichaka kidogo cha jamii ya kunde, uliofunikwa na vinyweleo laini vya kijivu. Majani yake yamegawanyika katika jozi kadhaa za vijani vyembamba, kama ya mbaazi. Una maua madogo ya jamii ya kunde, ya waridi hadi zambarau, na maganda membamba yenye vinyweleo. Wadigo huutambua kwa majani yake.

where.en: It grows in grassland, bush, and on roadsides and old farmland across tropical Africa and Asia.
where.sw: Huota mbugani, vichakani, na kando ya barabara na kwenye mashamba ya zamani kote katika Afrika na Asia ya kitropiki.

culture.en: Both names compare the plant to *mbalazi*, the pigeon pea that farmers grow, and say it is the wild one. *Chibalazi mlungu* means 'pigeon pea of God': it grows under God's care rather than a farmer's. *Chibalazi cha nze* means 'pigeon pea of outside', because it grows out there and not in the field. *Chi-* marks it as smaller than the real crop. Pakia draws a wider point from names like these: Digo often name a wild plant after the crop it resembles, as with *mtungudza* (African eggplant) and its wild relative *mtungudza koma*.
culture.sw: Majina yote mawili yanaulinganisha mmea huu na *mbalazi*, mbaazi wanayolima wakulima, na yanasema kuwa huu ni wa porini. *Chibalazi mlungu* lina maana ya 'mbaazi ya Mungu': huota chini ya uangalizi wa Mungu badala ya mkulima. *Chibalazi cha nze* lina maana ya 'mbaazi ya nje', kwa sababu huota huko nje na si shambani. *Chi-* huonyesha kuwa ni mdogo kuliko zao halisi. Pakia inatoa hoja pana zaidi kutokana na majina kama haya: mara nyingi Wadigo huupa mmea wa porini jina la zao unalofanana nalo, kama ilivyo kwa *mtungudza* (ngogwe) na jamaa wake wa porini *mtungudza koma*.

names.en: Pakia records *chibalazi chanze* (written in full as *chibalazi cha nze*) and *chibalazi mlungu*. The second is shared with Duruma. Mgombato also lists *chibalazi mlungu*, but identifies it as a different legume, *Desmodium velutinum*, and glosses it in Swahili as *mpacha* or *nfungamwitu*. The name may cover more than one wild pea-like plant.
names.sw: Pakia inarekodi *chibalazi chanze* (kikiandikwa kamili *chibalazi cha nze*) na *chibalazi mlungu*. Jina la pili linatumika pia kwa Kiduruma. Mgombato pia inaorodhesha *chibalazi mlungu*, lakini inalitambua kama mmea mwingine wa jamii ya kunde, *Desmodium velutinum*, na inalitafsiri kwa Kiswahili kama *mpacha* au *nfungamwitu*. Huenda jina hili linahusu zaidi ya mmea mmoja wa porini unaofanana na kunde.
